newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PolyDoc shares debut on Amsterdam's NMAX.
newsitem.headline: PolyDoc shares debut on Amsterdam's NMAX.

text.p: Shares in information software firm PolyDoc made their debut on the New Market of the Amsterdam Exchanges (NMAX) at 1100 GMT on Tuesday.
After 35 minutes there was still no trade in the Amsterdam-listed shares, but they were quoted at 10 guilders.
Earlier, the company announced it had placed 528,000 shares at 8.70 guilders each after a bookbuilding procedure.
The NAMX is a new trading segment of the Amsterdam Exchanges for young and fast growing companies with international ambitions. PolyDoc was set up in 1993 by British entrepreneur Berry Mence.
The company developes software modules aimed at managing and streamlining large organisations.
It made a net loss of 662,000 guilders on turnover of 1.87 million guilders in 1995. The 1996 results are due on April 16.
PolyDoc's shares were listed on London's Alternative Investment Market (AIM) in September 1996, when some some 4.5 million shares were floated.

Huub Maas, a spokesman for the NMAX placement lead manager Rabo Securities, said last Wednesday that PolyDoc expected a loss of less than 500,000 stg for 1996, but added prospects for 1997 and later were very positive.
